groups.rationale: Explicit adapter selection, optional JAR supervision, distinct error/value/lifecycle contracts and measured connection-specific acceptance are local architecture policy.
groups.protected_contract: Keep Java outside the direct path, prohibit implicit transport fallback, preserve protocol error provenance and independently verify optional Terminal adapters.

groups.rationale: Optional manual live verification, private response retention, differential replay and release evidence gates are local project policy.
groups.protected_contract: Keep live credentials and service calls out of CI; preserve explicit consent, finite query/capture scope, private provenance and independent enhancement review during upstream updates.

groups.rationale: Observed Python authentication POST fields and terminal header; compatibility evidence, not a new Rust policy.
groups.protected_contract: Preserve the observed request mapping until an evidenced upstream revision changes it.

groups.rationale: Inherited credentials, environment and response shape combined with Rust library boundaries, explicit validation/discovery, bounded requests and failed-login behavior.
groups.protected_contract: Preserve standalone auth/session reuse, explicit credentials and discovery policy, input/response validation, timeout defaults and no save after failed auth independently of upstream packaging changes.

groups.rationale: Rust CLI, native persistence, local status/logout, redaction, transport safety, lifecycle and verification/performance policy are independent product obligations, not Python parity.
groups.protected_contract: Retain each canonical auth policy, including runtime scope, store format/identity, precedence and diagnostics, unless deliberately migrated with independent tests.

groups.rationale: Observed EOD request, session, compression, values and finite RPC semantics are combined with typed Rust entry points, local date validation, exact prices, strict schema/timezone checks and explicit partial/error behavior.
groups.protected_contract: Preserve typed validation, exactness, schema/order/null decisions, safe terminal/error distinctions and the Table timestamp contract. Add numeric delivery through PERF requirements; do not silently replace the Table representation during a vendor update.

groups.rationale: Local symbol policy, pull/fused lifecycle, deadlines/cancellation, redaction, bounded allocation/work and Rust-native verification/traceability are selected Rust behavior.
groups.protected_contract: Keep every local limit, lifecycle and verification obligation during wire upgrades. Unmeasured defaults remain explicit gates rather than disappearing or being asserted implemented.

groups.rationale: Library dependency, optional storage and adapter boundaries are Rust architecture decisions.
groups.protected_contract: Vendor changes must not pull application, persistence or Python policy into the core/fast path.

groups.rationale: Numeric batch delivery, explicit presentation and measured hot-path acceptance go beyond Python dataframe parity.
groups.protected_contract: Keep optional conversion, exact numeric semantics, bounded work and calibrated performance regression decisions independently of source package updates.

groups.rationale: Independent change control and optional local projection/filtering are Rust capabilities, not invented upstream fields.
groups.protected_contract: Keep opt-in deterministic transform semantics and explicit enhancement impact review; no implicit server pushdown or Python callback in native delivery.

adrs.rationale: Explicit direct/REST/WebSocket boundaries, optional Terminal process ownership and independent entitlement/performance evidence.
